dependencies.description: An architecture-matched Wintun DLL in the trusted deployment location.
The compatible signed split-driver service, installed and started by deployment tooling.
A Windows identity that can change TUN, route, DNS, WFP, and driver state.
A usable family-specific Windows underlay selected by the backend.

platforms.reason: Native Almagest qualification evidence is not yet available.
A separate native Windows 11 amd64 qualification run is required.
A native arm64 host qualification run is required; emulation does not qualify this entry.

features.mapping: sysnet system allocate-ip and allocate-subnet for IPv4 and IPv6
features.notes: Allocation remains subject to live host conflicts.

features.mapping: almagest/Tun; create, create-named, set/get addresses, set/get routes, and set MTU for IPv4, IPv6, and dual stack
features.notes: The backend owns the adapter and only reconciles its owned state.

features.mapping: sysnet tun/default-tun rename
features.notes: Requests must fail before mutation. Named creation is supported but later rename is not.

features.mapping: almagest/DefaultTun; non-strict full routing for IPv4, IPv6, and dual stack
features.notes: This is not a persistent kill switch. More-specific routes can take priority.

features.mapping: almagest/DefaultTun rebuild on address, route, DNS-address, or MTU change; in-place SetDNS provider replacement
features.notes: The backend reports default-TUN property mutation as unsupported; the node must rebuild instead.

features.mapping: sysnet default-tun include routing profile
features.notes: Almagest must not translate include rules into exclusions.

features.mapping: sysnet strict full/include/exclude default-tun profiles
features.notes: The strict menu field must show the unsupported state.

features.mapping: sysnet default-tun source-routes operation
features.notes: Graphs that require source routes must fail clearly.

features.mapping: almagest/OutNet; IPv4/IPv6 TCP and UDP dial/listen, interfaces, and resolver operations
features.notes: Loss of the selected underlay makes the operation unavailable. There is no unrestricted fallback.

features.mapping: sysnet OutNet multicast and raw-socket operations
features.notes: Ambiguous generic wildcards and IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are also rejected.

features.mapping: sysnet OutDNS UDP/TCP query operations through bound OutNet sockets
features.notes: No usable numeric upstream makes the operation unavailable.

features.mapping: almagest/LocalNet; IPv4/IPv6 loopback TCP and UDP
features.notes: Resolution fails if any result is not loopback. Wildcard listeners bind explicitly to loopback.

features.mapping: almagest/DefaultTun managed UDP/TCP DNS proxy, interface DNS configuration, and SetDNS
features.notes: Managed adapter DNS is not system-wide DNS enforcement. SetDNS(nil) drops requests.

features.mapping: win-exe-tree in non-strict default-tun exclude rules
features.notes: The feature is unavailable when the split driver is missing, stopped, incompatible, or owned by another controller.

features.mapping: win-pid TCP/UDP ownership matcher for IPv4 and IPv6
features.notes: Matching is best effort. Unknown or ambiguous ownership is not a confirmed nonmatch.

features.mapping: win-exe-path TCP/UDP ownership matcher for IPv4 and IPv6
features.notes: Matching is best effort and is not a security boundary.

features.mapping: Linux comm, exec, cmd, pid, user, uid, group, and gid semantics
features.notes: A saved Linux rule stays visible for repair and is not translated to a Windows rule.

features.mapping: almagest/Tun and almagest/DefaultTun class visibility from sysnet create capabilities
features.notes: Unknown permits a final backend check. Unavailable and unsupported do not.

features.mapping: TUN name, strict, include, exclude, rule type, and validation menu states
features.notes: Unavailable and unsupported fields show a reason and cannot be applied.

features.mapping: autocomplete for win-exe-tree rule values
features.notes: Manual absolute local drive-letter paths remain supported.

features.mapping: almagestd native SystemIntegration selection on Windows
features.notes: Windows now selects the native backend. Qualification remains unavailable until all required native core and E2E evidence exists.

features.mapping: ProgramData/LocalAppData config and storage, Windows ACL validation, durable writes, and snapshots
features.notes: Milestone 4 supplies the Windows permission and path model.

features.mapping: almagestd and almagest-cli local named-pipe administration
features.notes: Step 12 supplies the local transport, ACLs, client owner verification, and user/service endpoint separation. Qualification remains unavailable until the required native and E2E evidence exists.

features.mapping: owner-filtered panel, HTTP API, WebSocket, and diagnostics
features.notes: Step 13 supplies an optional best-effort Windows client-process user SID filter and warns when web admin is enabled without it. It is not strong authentication. API tokens are outside the Windows backend scope. Qualification remains unavailable until the required native and E2E evidence exists.

features.mapping: console execution, Service Control Manager execution, unified shutdown, and checked cleanup
features.notes: Service registration remains outside the daemon. Milestone 6 supplies SCM integration.

features.mapping: command-node child and descendant cleanup with Windows process containment
features.notes: Step 15 supplies suspended-start, kill-on-close Job Object behavior for protected commands and rejects Unix credentials before launch. TorDriver uses the same protected gobox service as other subprogram owners. Its off, auto, and strict modes have Tor protocol and traffic evidence under ordinary and elevated identities on Windows Server 2022 amd64. The privileged native gate also verifies CryptoAPI entropy and real Tor control-port startup under elevated and LocalSystem identities. Windows native v1 uses a Low-integrity write-restricted token and reports its documented host-network and filesystem-view exclusions. Windows 11 and arm64 still need separate qualification, and this matrix entry remains unavailable until all required native and E2E evidence exists.

features.mapping: Windows machine/current-identity certificate authority discovery
features.notes: Step 16 enumerates public certificates from the daemon identity's CurrentUser\Root and LocalMachine\Root stores without changing explicit trust selection. Native identity suites verify discovery, reload, cleanup, and source deduplication. Qualification remains unavailable until all required native and E2E evidence exists.
